title: [finding] pr-automation.yml's "WHICH LEVEL" prose still says "no check computes it" and "the two remaining levels are yours" — the clause-② level axis has computed it since #16055, and the refusal message points authors at this sentence
body:
Filed by the dev seat on #16361 (session `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`, PR #16945) as an out-of-scope finding. ⛔ **No severity asserted, no domain routing — that is triage's.** ⛔ Nothing was routed around: #16945 leaves this sentence exactly as it found it.

## The sentence

`.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, the `Check Changeset` step, closing the "WHICH LEVEL" prose block (measured at `9a89a0040d`, around line 725):

```
               ... The 64 historical `patch` precedents are
               pre-rule and nothing is retro-fixed. This is prose, not a gate -- no
               check computes it; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major` and
               says why in its header, and the two remaining levels are yours.
```

## Why it is false, and what following it costs

Both clauses were true when written. #16055 landed the LEVEL axis in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, and since then:

- **"no check computes it"** — a check does. `judgeLevel` mechanizes the maintainer ruling of 2026-09-04 (decision batch #35, on #15294) for every PR that declares clause ② `yes`.
- **"the two remaining levels are yours"** — they are not, on a clause-②-declaring PR. `patch` on the wrong package is refused with exit 1.

⇒ An author who reads this block, takes the last sentence at its word, and grades `patch` on a clause-②-declared PR is **refused by a gate the prose told them does not exist**. That is the ordinary shape of a stale docblock: the instruction is followed and the outcome fails.

⭐ **It is on the path a refusal creates, which is why it is worth a card rather than a shrug.** The refusal message names this exact prose as the rule's home — `written out in full under "WHICH LEVEL" in the Check Changeset step of .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` — so the reader most likely to arrive at this sentence is the one who has *just been refused by the check it denies*. #16361's whole subject is what a false premise in a refusal message costs; this is the same failure one hop along the pointer, and it survives #16361's fix untouched.

## What it is NOT

⛔ Not a request to weaken or restate the ruling — the ruling is right and #16361 did not contest it either. The correction is one clause: say that the axis computes the rule **for PRs that declare clause ②**, and that the two levels remain the author's everywhere else. The scope of what the gate does and does not judge is stated precisely in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s own header and in `judgeLevel`'s verdict table.

⚠️ Not measured by this seat: whether any other prose in that step, or in `AGENTS.md`, carries the same pre-#16055 claim. Only the sentence above was read.

## Adjacent, not duplicated

- **#16361** (this seat's card) — the *grain* the level rule is applied at. Landed as PR #16945; ⛔ does not touch this workflow prose.
- **#16713** — the same axis is blind to nested packages (`packages/*/src/**` matches one path segment). A different defect in the same predicate; ⛔ neither subsumes this one.
